Discharge Instructions:
You were hospitalized after your ERCP procedure for nausea, 
hypoglycemia and abdominal pain.  You need to return in ___ to 
have the pancreatic stent removed.  Please note your insulin 
dosing has been decreased.  Otherwise continue your previous 
medications as prescribed by your primary physician.  You have 
been given pain medication for your abdominal pain.  Do not take 
more than prescribed, drive or use machinery while taking this 
medication, as it can cause drowsiness and possibly confusion.

Please eat a bland diet, and follow up with your primary 
physician for medication refills and a checkup in the next two 
weeks. 

If you have low blood sugar (less than 60 mg/dL), drink juice or 
sugar tablets and go directly to the emergency room.  If you 
have have blood sugars in the 250 or greater range, 
consistently, please call your diabetes doctor for titration of 
your insulin.

Return to the emergency department if you have increasing 
abdominal pain, inability to eat or drink, fever greater than 
101, or any other alarming symptoms.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with chronic pancreatitis, dilated pancreatic
duct, pancreatic duct stones status post pancreatic duct stent placement on
___ with persistent symptoms

___.

FINDINGS:  Eight spot fluoroscopic images were obtained during ERCP performed
on ___ by Dr. ___ without a radiologist present.  The initial
images demonstrate a plastic single pigtail catheter in the main pancreatic
duct and an endoscope in the appropriate position with subsequent cannulation
and opacification of the main pancreatic duct.  A smooth stricture is noted in
the proximal portion of the pancreatic duct. Several subtle filling defects
are noted in the main duct which likely correspond to stones.  Please see the
corresponding ERCP report in OMR for further details.
